title: Exploratory end-to-end agentic retrieval with a semantic evidence gate
researchQuestion: When the frozen bounded agentic retrieval loop replaces only its deterministic evidence gate with GPT-5.4 Mini semantic assessment, does it reduce false acceptance of insufficient evidence without degrading answerable retrieval quality?
hypothesis: The semantic gate will reject high-similarity but insufficient evidence that the deterministic score-and-language gate accepts, causing targeted rewrites that preserve the frozen single-pass retrieval metrics while restoring zero false positives.

scientificPositioning.reason: The semantic assessor materially outperformed the deterministic gate but failed its frozen component thresholds. This experiment does not reverse that decision and cannot qualify the assessor for production by itself.
scientificPositioning.knownValidationReuse: The 54 general and 16 focused validation cases have informed earlier experiments. Historical baseline and deterministic-agentic results are reused without rerunning provider calls; the semantic-gated arm is new.
scientificPositioning.prohibitedClaim: Do not describe this as independent confirmation or as evidence that the semantic assessor passed its component benchmark.

singleChangedVariable: Evidence-sufficiency assessment inside the same bounded agentic loop: deterministic score-and-language gate versus GPT-5.4 Mini semantic gate.

frozenRetrievalControls.merge: deduplicate by chunk id, retain highest cosine score, then stable score ordering

agenticPolicy.insufficientAfterFinalAttempt: abstain and expose no evidence to generation

agenticDiagnostics: cases recovered by a second attempt
negative cases correctly converted to abstention
rewrite queries and retrieved evidence per attempt
operationalMetrics: mean, p95, and maximum incremental latency

advancementRule.decision: Advance the semantic-gated architecture only to a separately preregistered generation-quality validation if every quality, abstention, validity, cost, and latency check passes. Any failed check retains the single-pass architecture. Passing does not revise the failed component benchmark or enable production.

executionOrder: Commit this protocol before modifying the evaluator or loop integration.
Implement semantic-gate injection while leaving the deterministic default unchanged.
Add unit tests for semantic acceptance, semantic rejection, retry, final abstention, and provider failure.
Run a no-provider validation plan that verifies hashes, case counts, controls, and historical comparators.
Execute the semantic-gated arm once with cache-preserving retries only for transient technical failures.
Publish every case trace, metric, token, cost, latency, failure, and disagreement.
Apply the frozen advancement rule without post-hoc prompt or threshold changes.

generationBoundary.reason: Grounded answer generation would introduce a second changed variable and requires its own quality reference. This experiment ends at evidence selection or abstention.
generationBoundary.frozenFutureGenerator: GLM-5.2 BaseTen FP8 at low reasoning and 2048 maximum output tokens may be used only in a successor protocol if this experiment passes every advancement check.

executionOutcome.decision: Do not advance the current agentic architecture. The semantic gate preserved the frozen general retrieval metrics and eliminated false positives, but comparative evidence coverage remained 0.25 and side recall 0.375. None of the 39 second attempts recovered a case, so the planner added cost and latency without retrieval benefit.

postExecutionDiagnostic.scope: The four focused-positive cases that reached attempt two.
postExecutionDiagnostic.finding: For compare-c-cpp-dynamic-deallocation, the union of all chunks retrieved across both attempts contains canonical evidence for both technologies even though neither attempt alone does. The other three failed comparisons remain canonically incomplete after union.
postExecutionDiagnostic.naiveTop4Result: Globally sorting the cumulative union by cosine score and retaining four chunks loses the first-attempt C evidence, so naive cross-attempt accumulation does not recover the case.
postExecutionDiagnostic.hypothesisForFutureWork: A newly preregistered merge policy that accumulates evidence across attempts while reserving capacity per explicitly requested technology may recover complementary evidence without changing the planner, assessor, retrieval model, threshold, or top-k budget.
postExecutionDiagnostic.status: diagnostic only; no selection claim and no implementation in this experiment

limitations: The validation cases and historical comparators have informed earlier engineering decisions.
The semantic assessor failed its frozen AI-assisted component benchmark and is included only as an exploratory downstream stress test.
The component reference was AI-assisted and the three apparent false positives may be label errors.
The experiment measures evidence selection and abstention, not generated-answer quality.
The locked 24-case test remains untouched and cannot be used to repair or tune this candidate.
